info.description: How to read the map, how to use it, privacy and credits
info.tagline: Explore the sites of nuragic Sardinia
info.intro: An unofficial app to explore the nuraghi, domus de janas, giants' tombs, sacred wells and the other sites surveyed by the {project}, on a map that's easy to use on a phone too.

rows.privacy: No accounts, no tracking: what is shared
rows.about: The project, data, photos and code

info.sightLinesNote: Computed by CRS4 on the digital terrain model, they show how much of a 15 m tower can be seen from the other. You'll find them on each nuraghe's page, with “Show on the map”.
info.appearanceHint: Light or dark, as the device is. Outdoors at sunset, “Light” may read better.

tips.title: How to use it
tips.search: Search for a site by name or by town: the results are highlighted on the map.
tips.random: “Surprise me” picks any site, of the selected type if you've chosen one.
tips.tilt3d: “3D” tilts the map and brings out the terrain, with the sight lines drawn from one tower to another.
tips.tiltGesture: Drag up with two fingers to tilt the map and bring out the terrain, with the sight lines drawn from one tower to another; “2D” flattens it again.
tips.rotate: To rotate the map, use two fingers on a phone; on a computer, drag the compass, or drag the map with the right mouse button or while holding Ctrl. Tap the compass to put north back up.
tips.rotateMac: To rotate the map, use two fingers on a phone; on a Mac, drag the compass, rotate two fingers on the trackpad (in Safari) or drag the map while holding Control. Tap the compass to put north back up.
tips.directions: “Directions” opens the site in your maps app, where you can start the route.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.summary: NurNet+ has no accounts, uses no cookies or analytics and collects no data about you. To show you the map, photos and videos, though, the browser connects to other services, which receive your IP address.
privacy.locationText: It is used only if you tap {button} on the map and allow it in the browser. It shows you where you are: it stays on the device and is never sent or stored.
privacy.mapText: The map is provided by OpenFreeMap ({policy}) and the terrain by Amazon Web Services: they know the area you're looking at, not your location. The photos come from NurNet, which knows which nuragic sites you open; the app and the site data are hosted on GitHub Pages.
privacy.videoText: They load only if you tap “Load the video”; from then on the rules of {youtube} or {facebook} apply. The choice holds until the app is closed.
privacy.directionsText: The site's location is sent to your maps app, which works out the route under its own privacy rules.
privacy.deviceText: To work offline too, the app keeps a copy of itself and of the site data in the browser's storage, along with the appearance and language you chose, if you chose one. You can delete it in the browser's settings for this site.
